english: Let $\ell$ be the line of intersection of the planes $P_1: x+2y-z=3$ and $P_2: x-z=1$, and let $M$ be the line $\dfrac{x-1}{1}=\dfrac{y-1}{2}=\dfrac{z+3}{2}$. Among all the planes containing $\ell$, exactly one plane, say $\Pi_1$, has no point in common with $M$. Let $\Pi_2$ be the plane containing $\ell$ which is perpendicular to $\Pi_1$, and let $R$ be the point at which $M$ meets $\Pi_2$. Then the distance of $R$ from the line $\ell$ is
hindi: माना $\ell$ समतलों $P_1: x+2y-z=3$ तथा $P_2: x-z=1$ की प्रतिच्छेदन रेखा है, तथा $M$ रेखा $\dfrac{x-1}{1}=\dfrac{y-1}{2}=\dfrac{z+3}{2}$ है। $\ell$ को समाहित करने वाले सभी समतलों में से ठीक एक समतल, माना $\Pi_1$, का $M$ के साथ कोई उभयनिष्ठ बिन्दु नहीं है। माना $\Pi_2$ वह समतल है जो $\ell$ को समाहित करता है तथा $\Pi_1$ के लम्बवत् है, तथा $R$ वह बिन्दु है जिस पर $M$ समतल $\Pi_2$ से मिलती है। तब रेखा $\ell$ से $R$ की दूरी है
solution: A member misses $M$ only if its normal is perpendicular to $(1,2,2)$: $1+\lambda+4-2-2\lambda=0\Rightarrow\lambda=3$
$\Pi_1: 4x+2y-4z-6=0$, i.e. $2x+y-2z=3$; the point $(1,1,-3)$ of $M$ gives $2+1+6-3=6\neq0$, so $M\parallel\Pi_1$, $M\not\subset\Pi_1$
Key idea: $\Pi_1\perp\Pi_2$ and both contain $\ell$, so for a point of $\Pi_2$ the distance from $\ell$ equals its distance from $\Pi_1$
$R\in M$ and $M\parallel\Pi_1$, so this distance equals that of $(1,1,-3)$ from $\Pi_1$: $\dfrac{6}{3}=2$
solution_full: Every plane containing $\ell$, other than $P_2$, is $(x+2y-z-3)+\lambda(x-z-1)=0$ for some real $\lambda$, with normal $\overrightarrow{n}_\lambda=(1+\lambda,\,2,\,-1-\lambda)$.
A general point of $M$ is $(1+t,\,1+2t,\,-3+2t)$. Substituting in $P_2$: $(1+t)-(-3+2t)-1=3-t$, which vanishes at $t=3$, so $P_2$ meets $M$.
This has no root $t$ exactly when the coefficient of $t$ vanishes and the constant does not: $3-\lambda=0$ and $3+3\lambda\neq0$. So $\lambda=3$, and this is the only such plane.

Key idea: $\Pi_1$ and $\Pi_2$ are perpendicular planes meeting in $\ell$. For a point $R$ of $\Pi_2$, the perpendicular from $R$ to $\Pi_1$ lies in $\Pi_2$ and meets $\Pi_1$ on $\ell$, so it is also the perpendicular from $R$ to $\ell$. Hence the distance of $R$ from $\ell$ equals the distance of $R$ from $\Pi_1$.
Since $M$ is parallel to $\Pi_1$, every point of $M$ is at the same distance from $\Pi_1$. For $(1,1,-3)$: $\dfrac{|2+1+6-3|}{3}=2$.

Check by direct computation: $M$ meets $\Pi_2$ where $(1+t)-4(1+2t)-(-3+2t)+3=3-9t=0$, so $t=\dfrac13$ and $R=\left(\dfrac43,\dfrac53,-\dfrac73\right)$. A point of $\ell$ is $(1,1,0)$ and its direction is $(1,0,1)$; $\overrightarrow{AR}=\left(\dfrac13,\dfrac23,-\dfrac73\right)$, $\overrightarrow{AR}\times(1,0,1)=\left(\dfrac23,-\dfrac83,-\dfrac23\right)$, so the distance is $\dfrac{\sqrt{72}/3}{\sqrt2}=2$.
originality_note: New: the plane of the family is fixed by a non-incidence property (the only member that misses M), and the answer uses a hidden invariant: for perpendicular members through l, distance from l equals distance from the other plane, which is constant along M (way 4). Closest known: plane through the line of intersection of two planes parallel to a given line, and its distance from the line. Different because: the asked distance is from l to a point R on a second, perpendicular member, which reduces to the line-plane distance only through the invariant.

concept_use.Plane: Equations of Pi_1 and Pi_2, their normals, perpendicularity of two planes and the distance of a point from Pi_1.
concept_use.Line and a plane: M is parallel to Pi_1 (normal perpendicular to the direction of M, a point of M not on Pi_1) and meets Pi_2 at R; distance from the parallel line to the plane.
concept_use.Family of planes: All planes through l are (x+2y-z-3)+lambda(x-z-1)=0; lambda=3 gives Pi_1 and mu=-3/2 gives Pi_2.

stem_review: Read as a student: every point, line and plane is introduced before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently with sympy and numpy, is unique and equals the Answer Plan; the options have one form and exactly one is correct. Made precise that Pi_1 'has no point in common with M' (so a plane containing M is excluded), and that P_2 itself is also among the planes through l. Changed: replaced 'does not meet' by 'has no point in common with'.
key_step: Seeing that the distance of R from l equals the distance between the parallel line M and Pi_1 (perpendicular members through l).
justification: Two family conditions (parallel to M, perpendicular to Pi_1) and then either a direct point-line distance or the invariant; two ideas linked in a planes question. Comparable with 2026-P1-Q6 (L3), plane through a line perpendicular to another plane with distances.
